scenes.title: NTILE()
scenes.narration: NTILE distributes ordered rows into a specified number of roughly equal buckets, making it perfect for quartiles, deciles, and percentiles.

scenes.title: How NTILE(n) Works
bullets: Takes an argument n: the number of buckets
Orders rows by the ORDER BY inside OVER
Splits rows into n groups as evenly as possible
Extra rows go into the earliest buckets first
scenes.narration: NTILE takes a single argument, the number of buckets you want. It orders the rows according to your ORDER BY clause and then divides them into that many groups as evenly as possible. When the rows do not divide evenly, the remainder is spread across the earliest buckets, so the first buckets may hold one more row than the last ones.

scenes.title: Splitting Customers Into Quartiles
scenes.code:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  total_spend,
  NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS spend_quartile
FROM customers;
scenes.narration: This query ranks customers by their total spend and divides them into four buckets with NTILE of four. Quartile one contains the top spenders and quartile four the lowest. Because the ordering is descending, the most valuable customers land in the first bucket. If the customer count is not divisible by four, the earliest quartiles simply absorb the extra rows.

scenes.title: Building Buckets
steps: Sort all rows by the ORDER BY clause
Divide total row count by n
Fill buckets in order, largest first
Distribute any remainder to earlier buckets
scenes.narration: To build the buckets, the engine first sorts every row by your ordering. It then divides the total number of rows by n to find the base bucket size. Rows are filled into buckets in order, and any leftover rows from an uneven division are handed to the earliest buckets so the distribution stays as balanced as possible.

scenes.text: NTILE() powers segmentation — quartiles for spend, deciles for performance, percentile bands for scores — turning a continuous metric into ranked groups.
scenes.narration: NTILE is ideal for segmentation, turning a continuous metric like spend or score into ranked groups such as quartiles or deciles.
